# wl sync blocked: inbound worklog commits authored sorra@thewizardscode.com fail the author-identity gate

## Problem statement

`wl sync` in the SorraAgents checkout refuses to merge inbound worklog data when the incoming commits are authored by `sorra@thewizardscode.com` — a genuine project work identity used by the operator's other checkouts — because the author-identity gate accepted only the configured `user.email` (the GitHub noreply identity) plus the earlier `pi@local` exception. Work items and comments written from a `sorra@` checkout therefore stranded on the remote, and local work could not be published either (`wl sync --no-push` failed at the same pull/merge step).

## Users

- **Producer/operator (uses multiple checkouts).** "As the operator, I want worklog changes made from my `sorra@thewizardscode.com` checkout to merge on every agent host, so I do not have to re-author or hand-replay history per batch."
- **Agent sessions (Map, plan, audit).** "As an agent, I want `wl sync` to complete without `--allow-foreign-author`, so intake/plan/audit work is published instead of being stranded behind a gate refusal."

## Acceptance Criteria

- `wl sync` completes in the SorraAgents checkout (pull, merge and push) for inbound commits authored by `sorra@thewizardscode.com`, with no `--allow-foreign-author` override.
- The chosen policy is recorded in `syncAllowedAuthors` (`.worklog/config.yaml`) with a rationale comment, and the allow-list stays exact-email: no wildcards, no allow-all, empty author email still refused.
- The gate still refuses incident sentinel identities (`t@t.com` and the other `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS`), and no sentinel is ever added to the allow-list.
- Testing/validation: `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py` passes and continues to pin exact-email semantics, empty-email refusal and sentinel refusal.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Policy-only fix: the gate decision logic is unchanged, so the existing regression contract (`tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py`) remains authoritative.
- The allow-list may not be widened beyond an explicit email list — no wildcard, no allow-all, and the empty-author-email refusal is never bypassed.
- Work is pushed to `dev` only (`main` is promoted by the ship skill).

## Existing state (verified during intake, 2026-11-04)

- `.worklog/config.yaml` → `syncAllowedAuthors` contains `250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com`, `pi@local` and `sorra@thewizardscode.com`, with a comment recording that the last entry is the project's own work identity, not a sentinel (`4e1ec2b6f`, present on `dev` and `main`).
- `scripts/check_git_identity.py` gate logic unchanged; `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` untouched.
- `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py` drives the real exported `checkAuthorIdentity` gate and pins: `pi@local` accepted only via the allow-list, arbitrary foreign email refused, empty email refused even with `allowForeignAuthor`, sentinels never allow-listed. It reads the real project config, so the added entry participates in its membership/exactness assertions; the entry is not individually pinned by name.
- Verification this session: `wl sync --no-push` merged the inbound worklog data with no author-identity refusal (57 work items updated, 0 comments added, 0 `--allow-foreign-author` usage), so the four previously refused commits (`14e4cc89e`, `273325c35`, `23c315392`, `e8c0011a7`) now merge.
- Recurrence pattern: the same identity was refused on 2026-10-27 and again on 2026-10-29/10-31 (recurrence comment `SA-C0MVWICFTW001KBWQ`).

## Desired change

`sorra@thewizardscode.com` is accepted permanently as a permitted worklog-sync author through the project allow-list, while the gate's exact-email, empty-email and sentinel guarantees stay intact and continue to be covered by the existing regression tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.worklog/config.yaml` — `syncAllowedAuthors` entry plus the rationale comment (landed in `4e1ec2b6f`)
- `scripts/check_git_identity.py` — gate entry point and allow-list contract metadata; decision logic unchanged
- `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py` — allow-list contract regression tests (exact-email, empty-email, sentinel refusal)
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — gate rules and the allow-list remediation procedure

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `sorra@thewizardscode.com` is a real project identity, not a leaked/sentinel identity — it is absent from `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` and the producer explicitly chose to allow-list it rather than re-author history.
- **Risk (drift):** no test pins the individual `sorra@` entry; removing it would re-strand sync, but loudly (a gate refusal on the next sync), and the contract-level guarantees stay pinned — accepted.
- **Risk (scope):** further identities must each be a separately reviewed config change, not bundled into this item.
- **Risk (widening):** the allow-list is a project-wide policy widening; it stays bounded because matching is exact-email and empty emails are always refused.

## Related work

- SA-0MVLJDS04002KI1W — previous occurrence; the considered-but-rejected alternative (re-author the inbound `t@t.com` commits).
- SA-0MVGSB63F00803HK — precedent: allow-listing `pi@local` with the same bounded, exact-email approach.
- SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS — original author-identity gate incident and allow-list remediation guidance.
- SA-0MSW9RF740016WC7 — batch blocked by empty emails / `ross@example.com`.
- SA-0MVK4F993008D9S2 — `t@t.com`-authored commits on `refs/worklog/data`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview round was required: the seed description already contained the problem statement and ACs, and the open decision had been answered by the producer in the worklog record.

- Q: "How should the four inbound `sorra@thewizardscode.com` worklog commits be handled — (1) allow-list the identity, (2) re-author the commits to the configured GitHub identity, or (3) another machine/agent identity policy?" — Answer (producer, plan session `herdr-1793454596-4112787-24238`, 2026-10-31): option 1, add the identity to the allow-list. Source: worklog comment `SA-C0MVWIN02D006Y7YM`. Research: the rejected alternative (re-authoring, the SA-0MVLJDS04002KI1W playbook) would fix this batch only and recur on the next push from a `sorra@` checkout.
- Q: "Is `sorra@thewizardscode.com` a genuine identity or an incident sentinel?" — Answer (agent research): genuine project work identity; it is not listed in `scripts/check_git_identity.py::INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` and the config comment records it as the project's own work identity. Evidence: `.worklog/config.yaml`, `scripts/check_git_identity.py`.

# plan Key Files parser misses the bold-inside-heading form

**discovered-from:SA-0MVWO79DA006FYCQ** (producer decision Q2 = B: fixed as a
linked follow-up, not folded into that item).

## Problem

`skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` parses the Key Files section with
`stripped.startswith("**Key Files:**")` (`_parse_key_files_section`, ~line 147)
and the same literal test in `validate_key_files_format` (~line 243). A
description that writes the section as a markdown heading with a nested bold
marker — `## **Key Files:**` — never matches, so the plan skill's completeness
validation treats the section as absent and `validate_key_files_format` either
reports success on an empty list or warns "section is present but contains no
valid file paths" depending on the code path.

Consumers hit this: 9 of 386 items in the `tce-the-rising` store use
`## **Key Files:**` (the face-off tie epic RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU and its eight
children).

## Desired change

1. Accept the same forms as the fixed implement-skill parser
   (SA-0MVWO79DA006FYCQ): H1–H6 heading + `Key Files` with optional bold marker,
   optional parenthetical qualifier (`(predicted)`), optional closing `**`/`:`
   and case-insensitive matching; plus whitespace/colon-tolerant bare
   `**Key Files:**` lines.
2. Keep the existing behaviour of stopping the section at the next Markdown
   heading (SA-0MTYMD1NQ009R6W2) and keep every currently accepted form working.
3. Consider extracting the matcher into one shared helper if the audit follow-up
   lands the same change (see below) — record that decision rather than

## Acceptance Criteria

  and for the currently supported bare `**Key Files:**` line — table-driven

- `validate_key_files_format` no longer reports a valid `## **Key Files:**`
  section as missing/empty, and still warns on a genuinely empty section.
- Section extraction still stops at the next heading/bold section marker.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code

# Release gate (merge-dev-to-main.sh) discards the runner JSON, so a dev→main release cannot say why the suite gate failed

Discovered-from: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (during `/skill:plan`).

## Problem

`skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` runs the full-suite release
gate as:

```bash
if python3 "$TEST_RUNNER" --scope full --strict-git-env 2>&1; then
```

The runner's machine-readable result is never requested and the exit code is
the only signal, so a slot-contention expiry (`slot_busy`), a killed suite
(`killed`) and a genuine red suite all produce the same message: "Full test
suite failed on the merged dev→main tree — the release is blocked." The
operator cannot tell "fix the code" from "wait for a slot / raise
`TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`", and a release attempt can burn hours of queue wait before
failing indistinguishably from a real regression.

The pre-push hook gets the equivalent fix under **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (its
AC2/AC3); this item is the same defect on the release path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The release gate consumes the runner's machine-readable result and reports the same `gate_reason=<code>` vocabulary the pre-push hook uses.
- [ ] A slot-contention or killed-run failure prints a distinct message with the remediation hint (wait then re-run, or raise `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`), while a red suite keeps its current message.
- [ ] The gate still fails closed (non-zero exit, no release) in every failure case, and `SHIP_TEST_SKIP=1` still bypasses it.
- [ ] A hermetic test (following `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py`) pins the classification for slot contention, killed and red-suite cases.

## Notes

- Reuse the shared classifier introduced by SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI rather than a second copy; this item is deliberately **not** a child of it so the release path can ship independently.
- UK English throughout.

## Problem

`tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` (added in v0.1.25) builds a fixture release repo and drives `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` with a stubbed suite runner. Under a clean shell the module is green (verified: `run_tests.py --scope full --force` at tree a9b008ead → 5820 passed). Under the **pre-push hook** (i.e. any push to `dev`/`main`) the same three tests fail:

```
FAILED tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py::TestGreenGate::test_green_gate_invokes_full_scope_and_release_proceeds
FAILED tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py::TestRedGate::test_red_gate_blocks_release_before_pr
FAILED tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py::TestMissingRunnerFailClosed::test_missing_runner_fails_closed
FileNotFoundError: .../runner-marker.txt   (the stubbed runner was never invoked)
```

Root cause: git exports `GIT_DIR` (and the suite gate may export `GIT_INDEX_FILE`) into hook environments; the fixture repo's git commands then resolve against the *live* checkout instead of the fixture, so `merge-dev-to-main.sh` short-circuits and the suite gate never runs. This is the same class as SA-0MVYS34QF000AWQX (node fixtures inheriting the finish gate's `GIT_INDEX_FILE`).

**Consequence:** the pre-push full-suite gate is red for every `dev` push, so `dev` cannot be synced with `main` after a release (hit during the 2026-11-02 v0.1.25 release; the sync required `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` with a separately verified green tree).

## Impact

Users can now push `dev` after a release without `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`, enabling automated `dev`→`main` promotion to complete without manual intervention.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` scrubs the ambient git environment (`shared.git_sandbox.fixture_git_env()` or equivalent) for both the fixture repo construction and the merge-script subprocess, so it passes when run from a git hook.
2. A regression test proves the module passes with `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_INDEX_FILE` set to the live repository.
3. `git push origin dev` (fast-forward) succeeds without `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` after the fix.
4. Full suite green in both a clean shell and a hook-like environment.

## Related

- SA-0MVYS34QF000AWQX — same leak class for node fixtures.
- SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42 — audit/producer-review churn (unrelated, same release session).

# Standup more focused on user experience (re-homed from ContextHub)

> **Provenance:** re-homed from ContextHub epic WL-0MW397N0Z002AYWP per producer
> decision (Option A). The standup skill source of truth lives in this
> (SorraAgents) repository — `skill/standup/` — which `~/.pi/agent/skills`
> symlinks to. The ContextHub copy is closed as moved.


## Problem statement

The daily standup report is currently a dry, flat bullet list of work items
("things done" + technical summaries), which is hard to read aloud and does
not convey what the user gained from the work. The output should be grouped
into meaningful categories, with each completed item described as a
single sentence about its impact on the user experience — without work item
IDs.

## Users

- The operator, who reads/listens to the daily standup (TTS) and wants a
  readable narrative of what changed and why it matters to the user.
- Agent sessions that generate standups and need clear, stable instructions
  for turning the script's structured data into the grouped report.

Example user stories:
- "As the operator, I want the standup grouped by areas such as 'User
  experience when doing Foo' and 'Back end stability under heavy load', so I
  can quickly grasp where progress happened and what each change means for
  users."
- "As the operator, I want each completed item described as one
  user-experience impact sentence without IDs, e.g. 'Improved the speed of
  user interactions with Foo by providing a one-click setup of the deck'."

## Desired change

1. **Categories** are chosen by the LLM (the invoking agent) at report time;
   labels are free-form (e.g. "User experience when doing Foo", "UI layout to
   improve access to key information"). No fixed taxonomy.
2. **Per-item impact sentences** come from a new explicit `## Impact` line in
   the work item description, written by the agent completing the work. Items
   without one (including all existing legacy items, which are **not**
   retrofitted) fall back to the current `Title — user story` phrasing.
3. **Grouped-paragraph format in every section** — "Yesterday I completed work
   on…", "Open critical items", "Additional focus items for today",
   "Regressions" and "Blockers" — each section grouped **independently**
   (categories are chosen per section, not per whole report).
4. The deterministic script (`generate_standup.py`) continues to fetch and
   compute the selection data; it also extracts each item's `## Impact`
   sentence into the structured output. The LLM (agent session) does the
   clustering and paragraph rendering, keeping the script testable and the
   agent output interpretable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `generate_standup.py` extracts the `## Impact` sentence from each item's
   description into a dedicated structured field (e.g. `impact`), available in
   `--json` output; a missing/malformed Impact section yields an empty field
   without error.
2. The rendered report is readable as a narrative: it organises each section's
   items into categories chosen by the LLM at report time, items are grouped
   **independently within each section**, and no work item IDs appear anywhere
   in the rendered report.
3. Within each category, every item is described as a single
   user-experience-focused sentence: the item's `## Impact` sentence when
   present, else the existing `Title — user story` phrasing (fallback).
4. The report remains first-person and TTS-friendly (spoken-form dates, no
   ID brackets/backticks/underscores in spoken lines) and stays within the
   ~2-minute read budget.
5. CLI behaviour is unchanged for consumers (flags, JSON schema superset,
   `--output-path` write path, sync-first, commit/push); existing tests keep
   passing with additions for the new `impact` extraction.
6. Work-item completion guidance (project AGENTS.md / implement skill / intake
   brief template) is updated so newly completed items carry an `## Impact`
   sentence describing the user-experience impact of the change.
7. Testing/validation: unit tests cover Impact extraction (present, absent,
   malformed) and the fallback; a golden-output test renders a sample report
   and asserts grouped sections, no IDs, and Impact-first sentences.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, the standup SKILL.md, and any wiki/docs entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The script stays deterministic (no LLM calls inside `generate_standup.py`) —
  clustering/rendering happens in the invoking agent session per Q4 answer.
- Existing completed items are NOT retrofitted with `## Impact` lines.
- Report must stay first-person, TTS-friendly, under ~2 minutes reading time.
- No work item IDs in the rendered output.
- Surgical scope: the Herdr selection ordering and data sources are untouched.

## Existing state

- `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` (installed to
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/`) renders a flat markdown report from the
  Herdr selection list; per-item text is `Title — user story/problem/summary`
  extracted heuristically from the description.
- Report structure: `## <project> Standup Report (date)` with sections
  "Yesterday I completed work on…", "Open critical items", "Additional focus
  items for today", "Regressions", "Blockers".
- Items already carry `Key Files` and (mostly) `As a …` user stories in their
  descriptions; there is no standard Impact field today.

## Desired change (implementation sketch)

- `generate_standup.py`: add `extract_impact(description)` (parse the
  `## Impact` section) and include `impact` in `normalize_item`/report data;
  keep `format_report` as a stable fallback for `--json` consumers and tests.
- `skill/standup/SKILL.md`: replace the "Report Structure" template with
  agent-rendered instructions: cluster each section's items into free-form
  categories, render one paragraph per category (one impact sentence per
  item), never render IDs, keep the TTS/first-person rules, note the
  `## Impact` / fallback rule.
- Work-item authoring guidance: add `## Impact` (one sentence,
  user-experience impact) to the completion conventions (implement skill
  output / AGENTS.md), so future standups have real impact sentences.

## Key Files

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/SKILL.md` — report template → clustered paragraph
  rendering instructions; source of truth `skill/standup/SKILL.md` in the
  SorraAgents repo.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` — add `## Impact`
  extraction + `impact` structured field; keep JSON/fallback compat.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_*.py` — new tests for
  Impact extraction, fallback, no-ID golden output.
- `AGENTS.md` (project + `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` global) / intake brief
  template — completed items gain an `## Impact` sentence.

## Related work

- **Create a podcast for standups (WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8)** — consumes the
  rendered standup report; ensuring the grouped narrative stays parseable/TTS-
  friendly matters for it.
- Completed standup infra (sync-first WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K, maintenance
  routines WL-0MVIDWJ090090J3Q, scheduled prompts WL-0MTMN7W63001FCQR) —
  unchanged; this is an output-format change.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: existing items are not retrofitted with Impact lines (fallback
  covers them). Confirmed by operator (Q5/A).
- Assumption: LLM clustering runs in the invoking agent session, not in the
  script (Q4/A). Risk: agent non-determinism → mitigations: keep deterministic
  data layer, document expected structure, golden output reviewed in tests at
  the data layer, SKILL.md instructions constrain clustering.
- Risk: paragraphs lengthen the report past 2 minutes → mitigation: the agent
  is instructed to keep each category paragraph tight and cap per-item
  sentences at one.
- Risk: Impact lines may be missing or low-quality → fallback + guidance
  update (AC6); scope-creep risk noted: no changes to Herdr selection or
  podcast pipeline (linked as related work, not scope).
- Risk: agents may accidentally include IDs → explicit "no IDs" rule in
  SKILL.md + golden-output test asserting absence (AC2).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How should categories be determined?" — Answer (operator): "C — LLM-chosen at report time (free-form labels)". Source: interactive reply (round 1, 2026-11-06).
- Q2: "Where does each item's impact sentence come from?" — Answer (operator): "A — explicit `## Impact` line written into work items at completion; the script reads it". Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q3: "Which sections get the new grouped-paragraph format?" — Answer (operator): "C — every section, but group independently within the sections". Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q4: "Where does the LLM clustering run?" — Answer (operator): "A — in the invoking agent session; script emits structured item data; SKILL.md instructs the agent to cluster and render". Source: interactive reply (round 2).
- Q5: "Items without an `## Impact` line?" — Answer (operator): "A — fall back to current Title — user story phrasing". Source: interactive reply (round 2).
- Assumption (confirmed implicitly): existing completed items are not retrofitted with Impact lines.

# Remote-observed push verdict in finish

Parent: **SA-0MUOOXH17004ZEFX** — `implement.py finish` reports `git push to dev failed` when the push actually landed.

Builds on the test-first slice (the hermetic baselines land first; this slice makes them pass
and removes their `xfail(strict=True)` markers).

## Goal

As an implementation agent, when the push command is killed at the timeout but `origin/dev`
already points at my commit, I want `finish` to record the completion comment and leave the
item `completed`/`in_review` instead of resetting it to `open`; and as the producer, when
`finish` does report a push failure I want the report to say whether the commit was verified
**absent** from `origin/dev` or whether verification itself could not run, so I know exactly
what recovery is needed.

## Context

`git_push_to_dev()` (`implement.py` L5629) spawns `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev` in
its own process group. On `TimeoutExpired` it process-group-kills the push and raises
`PushTimeoutError` (L4667); on a non-zero exit it raises `PushNonFastForwardError` for
non-fast-forward wording, otherwise logs `git push to dev failed` and returns `False`. There is
no post-failure remote check. `phase_finish()` Step 6 (L12011) maps a `False` return to
`RuntimeError("git push to dev failed.")`, posts a manual-push comment on `PushTimeoutError`,
and the outer `RuntimeError` handler resets the status to `open`; steps 6a–8 (post-push
ancestry assertion, cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync) and the
`StatusLifecycle(target_stage="in_review")` exit run only after a successful push.
`_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` (L11050) retries the push inside the worktree and has the
same false-failure exposure.

## Desired change

1. Add `_verify_commit_on_remote(cwd, commit_hash, timeout=...) -> bool | None`: resolve the
   full hash, read `origin`'s `refs/heads/dev` tip (`git ls-remote`), fetch that ref when the
   tip differs (bounded), and return `True` when `git merge-base --is-ancestor` says the commit
   is reachable, `False` when positively absent, `None` when the probe itself failed
   (network/auth/timeout).
2. Route every non-success push outcome through that probe. Recommended shape: have
   `git_push_to_dev()` raise a distinct "interrupted but verified landed" signal (or return an
   outcome object) rather than `False`/`PushTimeoutError`, so `phase_finish` can mark
   `steps.push.verified_after_failure`, comment, and continue on the success path;
   `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` handles the same signal on its retry.
3. Keep the conservative failure paths unchanged (`open`, manual-push comment, worktree
   retained) with the unknown-outcome wording when the probe returns `None`.
4. Extract the probe so the existing post-*success* ancestry assertion
   `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (L8084, SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U, now completed) reuses it
   rather than shipping a second divergent probe; note the reuse on both items.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev()` (L5629), `PushTimeoutError` (L4667), `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` (L11050), `phase_finish()` Step 6 (L12011), `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (L8084); new `_verify_commit_on_remote()` helper.
- `tests/test_implement_push_landed_detection.py` — the baselines from the test-first slice.
- `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` — interrupted-push coverage.
- `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` — retry-push path.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — the annotation noting the fake must keep resolving a published commit.

## Constraints

- **Positive verification only.** Never report success for a commit that was not observed on `origin/dev`; do not weaken the terminal-status read-back guarantee (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58).
- **No pre-push hook on verification.** The hook runs the full suite (~minutes); verification uses `ls-remote`/`fetch`/`merge-base` only and is bounded (recommended ~60 s). A verification fetch updates only remote-tracking refs, which the live-repo guard already excludes.
- **Ancestry, not equality.** Sibling sessions may push after ours; the commit is landed when it is an *ancestor* of the current `origin/dev` tip. Resolve the short hash from `git_get_commit_hash()` to a full hash before the ancestry check.
- **No force-push, no history rewrite, no `reset --hard`** of the shared main checkout; recovery stays additive.
- **Preserve existing behaviour:** non-fast-forward rebase-and-retry (WL-0MUYTCF4L000FX3M), worktree retention on genuine failure (WL-0MV533YSW004D1E1), pre-push main-checkout mutation guard, and `_sync_parent_branch` safe-skip semantics.
- **Report fields are additive.** `steps.push` keeps its existing `success`/`hash` keys (a cleanup test indexes the literal push step); the verified-landed marker is a new optional key, never a renamed or repurposed one.
- **No workflow-language change:** only which outcome (success vs failure) `finish` selects when the remote says the commit landed.
- **Source of truth:** the fix lands in this repository's `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`; the installed copy at `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/` picks it up only after `scripts/install_pi.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Single shared remote-verification probe.** A new `_verify_commit_on_remote(cwd, commit_hash, timeout) -> bool | None` helper in `implement.py` resolves the full hash (resolving the short hash returned by `git_get_commit_hash()`), reads `origin`'s `refs/heads/dev` tip (`git ls-remote`), fetches that ref when the tip differs (bounded, ~60 s), and returns `True` when `git merge-base --is-ancestor <full-hash> <remote-tip>` reports the commit reachable, `False` when positively absent, and `None` when the probe itself failed (network/auth/timeout).
- **Remote-observed verdict before any failure report.** Before `finish` reports a push failure (`PushTimeoutError`, a process-group kill, or a non-zero `git push` exit that is not a non-fast-forward), every non-success outcome is routed through the probe — including the non-fast-forward retry push in `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` — and the verification is time-bounded and uses only ref/object plumbing (it must not invoke the pre-push hook or the test suite).
- **Verified landed is success, not failure.** When verification confirms the commit is on `origin/dev`, `finish` completes normally: it records the completion comment naming the commit, performs the existing success-path cleanup (process cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync), leaves the work item `completed`/`in_review` (terminal read-back still passes), and marks the report explicitly (`steps.push.verified_after_failure: true` plus the original error text) with an explanatory work-item comment.
- **Genuine failure and unknown outcome stay conservative.** When verification finds the commit absent from `origin/dev`, or verification itself fails (e.g. an `ls-remote` network error), `finish` still fails conservatively: the status resets to `open`, the manual-push/worktree recovery comment is posted, the worktree is retained, and the message/report distinguishes `push failed (commit not on origin/dev)` from `push outcome unknown (remote verification failed: <reason>)`, never claiming success without positive verification.
- **Ancestry, additive fields, preserved behaviour, no duplicate probe.** The commit is considered landed when it is an ancestor of the current `origin/dev` tip, never equality; the probe is extracted so the existing post-success ancestry assertion `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U) reuses it instead of shipping a divergent second probe; non-fast-forward rebase-and-retry, worktree retention on genuine failure, the pre-push main-checkout mutation guard and `_sync_parent_branch` safe-skip semantics keep working; and `report["steps"]["push"]` keeps its existing `success`/`hash` keys (new keys are additive only).

# Implement branch-aware worktree creation

## Goal

Make `phase_start` branch-aware so an existing child branch no longer fails
generically with "Failed to create worktree". The branch is either reused
(identical to / fast-forwardable from the parent branch) or the operator gets
an actionable error naming the stale branch and the recovery command.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the target child branch (`wl-<id>-<slug>`) already exists, `phase_start` no longer fails generically: it either reuses the existing worktree/branch (when that branch is at, or fast-forwardable from, the parent branch) or fails with an actionable error naming the stale branch and the recovery command.
- `git_worktree_add`'s boolean-only contract is extended so the caller can distinguish "branch exists" from other failures (`created` / `branch-exists` / `failed` verdicts), with the single `phase_start` call site updated and the source-order assertion in `tests/test_implement_node_modules_symlink.py` kept satisfied.
- Reuse path: a branch whose tip is an ancestor of (or equal to) the parent branch is fast-forwarded to the parent tip with `git branch -f` and registered with `git worktree add <path> <branch>` (no `-b`); the report sets `reused_branch: true` and `branch_fast_forwarded: true|false`.
- Unsafe path: a branch carrying commits not reachable from the parent branch (or from `origin/<parent_branch>`) is never reset or reused silently; `phase_start` fails with the branch name, the unique-commit count and the exact recovery commands, and resets the item to `open`.
- A branch checked out in another worktree is reported by name and never raced.
- The xfail markers added by "Test: Stale-branch recovery regression suite" for this behaviour are removed and the tests pass.

## Minimal Implementation (end-to-end slice)

- Introduce verdict constants + `branch_exists(repo_root, branch)` (via
  `git show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/<branch>`) and
  `_branch_reuse_verdict(repo_root, branch, parent_branch)` returning
  `identical` / `fast-forwardable` / `unique-commits`, plus
  `_branch_checked_out_in_other_worktree(repo_root, branch)`.
- Change `git_worktree_add` to return the verdict string; keep the call
  prefix `git_worktree_add(branch,` so existing source-order assertions hold.
- In `phase_start` step 7, when `not resumed` and `branch_exists`: compute the
  verdict, fast-forward when safe, then register the worktree from the
  existing branch; otherwise set `report["success"] = False`,
  `report["stale_branch"] = {branch, unique_commits, recovery_commands}` and
  return after resetting status to `open`.
- Report the decision under `report["steps"]["worktree_branch"]` so `parent`
  and `drive` reports surface why a start reused a branch.

## Constraints

- Never `git branch -f`, `reset` or delete a branch that has commits absent
  from the parent branch — reuse is limited to branches with no unique
  commits.
- Do not weaken the main-checkout placement guard, stash-hygiene gate, code
  freeze gate, or parent-tracking assertion.
- Preserve `--worktree-path` override semantics and the idempotent worktree
  resume path (`_is_worktree`).
- Re-running `start` after a successful reuse must be idempotent (no second
  branch, no second worktree, no duplicate comment).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_worktree_add`, new branch helpers, `phase_start` step 7
- `tests/test_implement_start_resume.py`
- `tests/test_implement_stale_branch.py` (added by the test-first child)
- `tests/test_implement_node_modules_symlink.py` (source-order assertion)

- Blocked by "Test: Stale-branch recovery regression suite" (test-first).

## Deliverables

- Verdict-returning `git_worktree_add` plus branch state helpers.
- `phase_start` reuse / fast-forward / actionable-error behaviour.
- Green regression tests for the AC3 matrix.

# Implement safe branch cleanup

## Goal

Stop a failed or aborted `start` from poisoning the next `start` with a
orphaned feature branch: clean up the branch this run created, remove the
abandoned branch on `abort` when it is safe to do so, and always report what
was removed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `start` that fails after creating the branch cleans up the branch it created; `phase_abort` removes the abandoned feature branch (with a guarded delete — never force-deleting a branch with unmerged commits that are the only copy) and reports what it removed.
- The failed-`start` cleanup also removes the worktree registration it created, so no half-created `.worklog/worktrees/wl-*` directory survives the failure.
- `phase_abort` discovers the abandoned branch by prefix (`refs/heads/wl-<item-id>-*`) rather than needing the item title, deletes it with `git branch -d` semantics only when it has no unique commits, and reports `branch_removed` / `branch_retained` with the reason and the recovery command.
- A branch that carries commits not reachable from the parent branch or `origin/<parent_branch>` is retained and named in the abort report and comment — never force-deleted.
- The xfail markers added by "Test: Stale-branch recovery regression suite" for this behaviour are removed and the tests pass.
- The full project test suite passes with the new changes (enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Minimal Implementation (end-to-end slice)

- New `_delete_branch_if_safe(repo_root, branch, parent_branch)` returning
  `{deleted, reason, unique_commits}` with reasons `deleted` / `not-found` /
  `unique-commits` / `checked-out-elsewhere` / `error`; unique-commit count is
  taken against both the local parent branch and `origin/<parent_branch>`.
- New `_discover_item_branches(repo_root, work_item_id)` via
  `git for-each-ref --format=%(refname:short) "refs/heads/wl-<id>-*"`.
- Wrap the post-`git worktree add` steps of `phase_start` so a failure after
  creation removes the worktree (guarded by `_remove_worktree`) and then
  deletes the branch this run created, reporting
  `report["cleanup"] = {worktree_removed, branch_removed, reason}`.
- In `phase_abort`, after the worktree removal and before
  `_restore_repo_state`, delete each discovered item branch that is safe and
  record the outcome on the abort comment.

## Constraints

- No blind `git branch -D`: deletion is only reached when the unique-commit
  count is zero, and a branch checked out in another worktree is never
  touched.
- Cleanup failures are logged and reported, never fatal to `abort`.
- Idempotent: a second abort finds no branch and reports `not-found` without
  error.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_delete_branch_if_safe`, `_discover_item_branches`, `phase_start` post-create failure path, `phase_abort`
- `tests/test_implement_abort_safety.py`
- `tests/test_implement_stale_branch.py` (added by the test-first child)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by "Test: Stale-branch recovery regression suite".
- Blocked by "Implement branch-aware worktree creation" (shares the branch
  helpers and must not conflict on the `phase_start` failure path).

## Deliverables

- Guarded branch deletion helper and item-branch discovery.
- Failed-start cleanup of the worktree and the branch it created.
- Abort-time branch removal/retention reporting.

# Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6)

## Problem statement

Implement sessions that run concurrently spend the overwhelming majority of their
wall-clock waiting on a single per-repository `flock`, because `implement.py finish`
holds that lock across its **whole** commit → fast-forward → push → post-push window
and the dev-push **pre-push hook runs the full test suite (~5.4 min)** inside it.
Every concurrent `finish` therefore serialises its expensive test run behind the
others. At the intended fan-out of **up to 6 concurrent sessions**, the sixth finish
queues behind five ~5-min full-suite runs.

## Evidence (2026-11-13, AI_Hell implement-skill sessions)

Analysed the 36 worktree sessions that started with the implement skill
(`~/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-AI_Hell-.worklog-*`):

- **668 min** summed session time over a **388 min (6.5 h)** wall-clock span —
  only **1.7x effective parallelism** at a **peak measured concurrency of 4**.
- **88–93%** of each long session's wall-clock was inside `bash` tool calls
  (waiting on processes), not model reasoning or edits.
- Time buckets: **wait_for_job 249 min (37%)** (215.9 min of it lock-waits),
  own `finish` 133 min (20%), scoped tests 57 min (9%), hand-rolled
  `sleep`/`grep` polling loops 48 min (7%).
- **57** "another run holds the repository lock" refusals; **46** observed
  lock-waits averaging **4.3 min** (median 5 min, **max 21.5 min**). Worst single
  tool call: **45 min** = a `for attempt in 1..8` retry loop absorbing five
  consecutive lock holders.
- **21** non-fast-forward rebase events, each creating a new tree that re-triggers
  the full-suite pre-push gate (9 full-suite gate runs today).
- 9 sessions were **no-ops** (3 messages, ~50 s) — drive retries that immediately
  gave up.

## Users

- **Operator** running a fan-out batch of up to 6 concurrent implement sessions
  (the intended operating point) on a single repository.
- **Implement-skill sessions** (leaf and driven child) whose `finish` currently queues
  behind other sessions' full-suite runs.
- **Producers/reviewers** who need the speed-up evidenced, not asserted.

User stories:

- As an operator running up to 6 concurrent implement sessions, I want `finish` to
  complete in minutes of real work rather than tens of minutes of serialised queueing
  behind other sessions' full-suite runs, so a fan-out batch finishes in roughly the
  time of one work item rather than the sum of all of them.
- As a driven child session, I want my single `finish` call to wait boundedly on the
  lock instead of scripting retry loops.
- As a producer, I want a recorded before/after measurement before the epic is closed.

## Goal

As an operator running up to 6 concurrent implement sessions, I want `finish` to
complete in minutes of real work rather than tens of minutes of serialised
queueing behind other sessions' full-suite runs, so a fan-out batch finishes in
roughly the time of one work item rather than the sum of all of them.

## Decomposition

The epic is decomposed into five child items; together they own every acceptance
criterion below.

1. Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock
   (SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4) — the single biggest time sink: stop holding the exclusive
   repository lock across the ~5.4 min full-suite gate.
2. Finish wait ergonomics: one bounded internal wait, no bespoke retry loops
   (SA-0MWFJS65O005JMJF) — replace fail-fast refusals plus agent-scripted retry loops
   with one bounded internal wait that reports the holder.
3. Stop rebase-induced full-suite re-runs on dev pushes (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC) — a lost
   push race currently pays the full suite again because the rebase produces a new tree.
4. Eliminate no-op drive retries that spawn and immediately give up
   (SA-0MWFJSCPT005BO2R) — 9 of 36 sessions did no work.
5. Measure the 6-way concurrent finish fan-out and record before/after analysis
   (SA-0MWFK10NH006QI7E) — verifies the outcome ACs against real session logs; blocked
   by items 1–4.

## Acceptance criteria

- Under a 6-way concurrent `finish` fan-out, no session spends the majority of its
  wall-clock blocked on the per-repository lock (measured: median lock-wait per session < 60 s; no single lock-wait > 5 min).
- The full test suite is never executed while a single global repository lock is held (proved by inspection + test).
- A waiting `finish` performs **one** bounded internal wait rather than N fail-fast round-trips, and the skill guidance contains no bespoke `for attempt ...; wait_for_job` finish retry loops.
- A concrete before/after measurement is recorded (same 36-session style analysis).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Safety invariants stay intact: single-owner mutation of the shared `dev` ref, the
  bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, and tree/provenance binding of gate verdicts
  (no verdict about a different tree/diff may be trusted).
- The dev-push gate keeps `scope=full` for release-critical refs — the speed-up must not
  weaken the release gate.
- Target concurrency is **up to 6**; designs are evaluated at that fan-out.

## Existing state

- `implement.py finish` acquires `<main-checkout>/.worklog/locks/main-checkout.lock`
  (`shared.repo_lock.RepoLock`) at Step 3c and holds it through push and post-push
  verification; `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` defaults to 0 (fail fast).
- `.githooks/pre-push` runs `run_tests.py --scope full --gate-commit <sha>` for
  pushes to `dev`/`main`, with a tree-keyed verdict cache (`fingerprint_kind="tree"`)
  and gate provenance lines, all of which execute inside the held finish lock today.
- Pushes to the shared `dev` ref lose the non-fast-forward race under concurrency; the
  rebase-and-retry path in `implement.py` produces a new tree and therefore a cache miss.
- `phase_drive` spawns one session per child; some spawns observe state that makes the
  child immediately terminal/blocked and exit as no-ops.

## Desired change

Concurrent `finish` runs overlap their expensive work instead of serialising on one
repository-wide critical section, and the epic's outcome is evidenced by a recorded
before/after session analysis.

## Impact

An operator can run a 6-way concurrent implement fan-out and have the batch finish in
roughly the time of one work item, instead of waiting for six serialised five-minute
test runs — while still shipping only fully tested commits.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` Step 3c lock window, push/rebase retry path, `phase_drive` spawn decisions
- `skill/shared/repo_lock.py` — `RepoLock` / bounded wait for `main-checkout.lock`
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — full-suite gate, `test` semaphore lane, tree-keyed verdict cache
- `.githooks/pre-push` — dev/main full-suite gate and cache mirroring
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — finish/wait guidance to update
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py`, `skill/implement/tests/test_lock_timeout_isolation.py`, `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — existing regression coverage to extend

## Related work

- Crash-safe per-repository finish lock (SA-0MVPZG3IQ009IJMO) — the lock/wait helper this epic shrinks the critical section of.
- implement.py finish: concurrent sessions orphan each other's commits via the shared local-dev fast-forward (SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY) — established the single-owner lock invariant.
- Hermetic regression tests for finish concurrency orphans (SA-0MVPZG01J0067PC2) — concurrency test patterns to reuse.
- Defer full suite to dev-push (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81) — why the full suite sits at the gate.
- Tree-keyed gate verdict (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV) — the cache that makes verdict reuse possible.
- Session-time analysis skill (SA-0MVIKL8U7003UACM) — this epic's measurement items should reuse/feed it.
- Post-fix slot-wait re-measurement (SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K) — precedent methodology for before/after measurement.
- Git transport is fragile under concurrent agent runs (SA-0MW22SEMV00230O5) — push-race prior art.

## Out of scope

- Trimming the full suite's own runtime / sharding / per-file caching, and raising
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` — those are per-project (AI_Hell) concerns, not framework.
- Changing changed-scope test selection.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** moving the suite out of the lock could let an untested tree reach `dev`;
  mitigation is the tree/provenance-bound verdict and the ancestry assertion, both
  preserved by the owning children.
- **Risk:** verdict reuse after a rebase could accept a genuinely different diff;
  mitigated by provable content equality plus a negative test.
- **Risk (scope creep):** building a general lock/push queue service is out of scope;
  the children take the smallest change that meets their ACs.
- **Assumption:** the measured symptom is lock serialisation, not per-project suite
  runtime — the baseline bucket analysis supports this (37% in `wait_for_job`, 215.9 min
  of it lock-waits).
- **Assumption:** sessions of comparable work-item size are available for the "after"
  measurement; otherwise a synthetic 6-way fan-out supplies it.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What concurrency target must the design satisfy?" — Answer (operator, 2026-11-13):
  "Up to 6 concurrent implement sessions." Source: analysis comment on this item
  (SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR).
- Q: "Is trimming the per-project full test suite runtime in scope?" — Answer (operator,
  2026-11-13): "No — per-project (AI_Hell) suite trimming, sharding and
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` changes are out of scope for this epic." Source: same comment.
- Q: "What is the evidence base for the problem statement?" — Answer: the 2026-11-13
  AI_Hell analysis of 36 implement-skill sessions (668 min summed over a 388 min span;
  1.7x effective parallelism; 46 lock-waits, median 5 min, max 21.5 min; 21 rebases;
  9 no-op sessions). Source: comment SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR and the "Evidence" section
  above.
- Q: "Does the epic already own a measurement/verification item?" — Answer (this intake,
  research: `wl list --parent SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1`): no — the four original children all
  change code, so the outcome ACs had no owner; child 5
  (SA-0MWFK10NH006QI7E) was created to own them.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4** – Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock (open)
- **SA-0MPVO6JNI006ESN0** – Triage dev-full-suite failures (run 26780355787) (completed)
- **SA-0MW6VXSF8004X1PK** – [test-failure] post-push full-suite verification: no valid full-suite cache entry — failing test (completed)

- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mvecqugf0064u81, 0mvpzg3iq009ijmo, 0mw22semv00230o5, accept, acceptance (+333 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mvecqugf0064u81, absorbing, accept, acceptance, acquires (+329 more)

`implement.py finish` acquires the per-repository `flock`
(`<main-checkout>/.worklog/locks/main-checkout.lock`) at Step 3c and holds it until
the `finally` block — covering commit → fast-forward local dev → **push** → post-push
verification. The dev push triggers `.githooks/pre-push`, which runs the **full test
suite** (`run_tests.py --scope full`, measured ~326 s / 5.4 min for AI_Hell) while the
lock is held. A read-only test run is therefore made part of the exclusive mutating
critical section, so every concurrent `finish` serialises its ~5-min suite behind the
others. This is the root cause of the 37% `wait_for_job` share and the 46 lock-waits
(median 5 min, max 21.5 min).

- **Operator** running a fan-out batch of up to 6 concurrent implement sessions.
- **Implement-skill session** whose `finish` currently spends most of its wall-clock
  waiting for the lock rather than doing work.

- As an operator running a 6-way fan-out, I want concurrent finishes to overlap their
  full-suite gate runs so the batch finishes in roughly the time of one work item
  rather than the sum of all of them.
- As an implement-skill session, I want the exclusive repository lock to cover only
  the short mutating window, so my `finish` is not blocked for another session's
  ~5-minute test run.

## Goal

As an operator running concurrent implement sessions, I want the full-suite gate to
run **without** holding the exclusive repository lock, so concurrent finishes overlap
their test time instead of queueing on it.

## Approach

  main-checkout lock (the tree-keyed cache already exists — reuse it), or run the
  suite under only the shared `test` semaphore lane, not the repo lock.

  ancestry assertion (should be seconds).

  ref, the bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, and the tree/provenance binding of

- The full test suite is never executed while `main-checkout.lock` is held (asserted
  by a test that observes lock state across the suite invocation).
- The lock-hold window in a green `finish` is bounded and does not include the
  full-suite duration (measured/asserted in a test or documented metric).
- A concurrent-finish integration test shows the second finish's wait is materially
  shorter when the first is running the full suite (no longer serialised on suite
  time).
- No regression in the existing finish-concurrency / ancestry-assertion tests.
- At least one automated test proves the new gate/lock ordering (lock state observed
  while the suite runs, and a green finish whose lock window excludes the suite).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- `.githooks/pre-push` always runs `run_tests.py --scope full` for pushes to

# Finish wait ergonomics: one bounded internal wait, no bespoke retry loops

Parent: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1).

## Problem statement

`IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` defaults to 0 (fail fast). When the lock is held, the
agent must re-enter the queue itself, so the skill guidance teaches a hand-rolled
`for attempt in 1..8; implement.py finish ... ; wait_for_job.py --pid <holder> ...`
loop. In the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis this pattern produced the single worst tool
call — **45 minutes** absorbing five consecutive lock holders — and accounted for a
large share of the 37% `wait_for_job` time plus 48 min (7%) of separate `sleep`/`grep`
polling loops. Each fail-fast refusal is also a wasted model round-trip.

## Users

- **Operator** running a fan-out batch: wants predictable, minimal waiting per session.
- **Implement-skill session** that currently has to script retry loops around
  `implement.py finish`.

User stories:

- As an implement-skill session, I want one `finish` call to wait internally on the
  lock (bounded, with progress) so I do not burn model round-trips on retry loops.
- As an operator watching a batch, I want a waiting session to report who holds the
  lock and to fail with an actionable message only when the bound expires.

## Goal

As an operator, I want a waiting `finish` to perform **one** bounded internal wait on
the flock (with progress), instead of the agent scripting fail-fast retry loops around
it, so concurrent finishes do not multiply round-trips and confusing logs.

## Approach

- Make a positive bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` the guidance default (or
  document setting it) so `finish` waits internally on the flock up to a generous
  bound, emitting progress.
- Remove the `for attempt in ... ; implement.py finish ... ; wait_for_job` retry-loop
  guidance from the implement skill; replace with the single bounded-wait instruction.
- Ensure the internal wait reports the holder and honours `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` cleanly.

## Acceptance criteria

- `implement.py finish` with a positive `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` waits on the
  lock internally within the bound, reporting the holder, and fails with an
  actionable message only when the bound expires.
- The implement skill docs contain no bespoke finish retry-loop pattern; they instruct
  a single bounded wait.
- A waiting `finish` performs **one** bounded internal wait rather than N fail-fast round-trips, and the skill guidance contains no bespoke `for attempt ...; wait_for_job` finish retry loops.
- A test covers: lock held → `finish` waits → holder releases → `finish` proceeds
  (no fail-fast refusal).
- Regression test that the wait is bounded (never hangs) and is signal-safe.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The wait must stay bounded: a configured timeout always terminates the wait with an
  actionable refusal naming the holder and the lock path.
- `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` must release the held lock and the child lock and exit cleanly
  (no orphaned locks).
- Default behaviour must stay safe for unattended sessions: a positive bound must not
  be able to wedge a batch indefinitely.
- Out of scope: changing the single-owner lock semantics or removing the lock.

## Existing state

- `DEFAULT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT = 0.0` (fail fast), env `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`,
  read by `_finish_lock_timeout()`; the bounded wait lives in
  `shared.repo_lock.RepoLock` via `acquire_main_checkout_lock`.
- The implement skill documents the current fail-fast behaviour, and sessions work
  around it with `for attempt ... ; wait_for_job.py --pid <holder>` loops.
- Lock holders are recorded with pid/host metadata, so the holder can already be named
  in a refusal.

## Desired change

`finish` performs one bounded internal wait with progress and holder reporting; the
skill guidance describes that single call instead of a bespoke retry loop.

## Impact

An operator's concurrent batch stops multiplying model round-trips and multi-minute
tool calls on lock contention: a waiting session reports who holds the lock and
proceeds automatically once released.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `DEFAULT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `ENV_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `_finish_lock_timeout()`, `acquire_main_checkout_lock` call in `phase_finish`
- `skill/shared/repo_lock.py` — bounded wait implementation and holder reporting
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — guidance that must lose the bespoke retry-loop pattern
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py` and `skill/implement/tests/test_lock_timeout_isolation.py` — test homes for the wait behaviour
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — timeout documentation

## Related work

- Parent epic: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1)
- Crash-safe per-repository finish lock (SA-0MVPZG3IQ009IJMO) — the lock/wait helper.
- implement test suite inherits IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT from the ambient environment and hangs for hours (SA-0MVY0G5EH000LIMB) — timeout inheritance hazard to keep in mind.
- Sibling item: Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock (SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4) — the other half of lock-wait reduction.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (scope creep):** building a general-purpose lock queue service is out of scope;
  this item is one bounded wait inside `finish`.
- **Risk:** a long default bound could make an unattended batch appear hung; mitigation:
  progress output plus a clear expiry message, and the default chosen deliberately
  (documented) rather than "infinite".
- **Assumption:** the holder pid/identity metadata recorded by `RepoLock` is sufficient
  to name the holder in progress output.
- **Assumption:** removing the retry-loop guidance from the skill does not break driven
  sessions, which call `finish` once per child.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required for this item. Evidence base: 2026-11-13 AI_Hell
36-session analysis on the parent epic (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1, comment
SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR), including the 45-minute worst-case tool call and the 48 min of
`sleep`/`grep` polling. Researched in the repository: `_finish_lock_timeout()` /
`DEFAULT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` and the bounded
wait in `skill/shared/repo_lock.py`.

# Stop rebase-induced full-suite re-runs on dev pushes

Parent: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1).

## Problem statement

Because concurrent finishes push to the shared `dev` ref, pushes frequently lose the
non-fast-forward race: in the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis there were **21** rebase
events. Each rebase rewrites the commit onto a new base, producing a **new tree**, which
misses the tree-keyed gate cache and **re-runs the ~5.4-min full suite** inside the
lock. So a single work item can pay the full-suite cost repeatedly (e.g. AH-0MWEZZE5U,
AH-0MWEYVRUX and others showed 2–3 rebase rounds each).

## Users

- **Operator** running a concurrent fan-out batch into `dev`.
- **Implement-skill session** that loses the push race and today pays another full-suite
  run after rebasing.

User stories:

- As an implement-skill session that lost the push race, I want to rebase and push
  without re-running the full suite, because my change content did not change.
- As an operator, I want the number of full-suite gate runs in a batch to stay close to
  the number of work items, not a multiple of it.

## Goal

As an operator, I want a rebased push not to re-run the full suite when the change
content is unchanged, so a lost push race costs seconds, not another 5 minutes.

## Approach (options to weigh)

- Serialise dev pushes (a short push queue / fast-forward retry that rebases only the
  ref, reusing the already-green tree verdict where the tree is provably identical).
- Or key the gate verdict on the **commit's change set / content hash** rather than the
  full tree, so a pure rebase (same diff, different base) reuses the verdict.
- Or batch dev advancement so a batch is rebased once.

## Acceptance criteria

- A push that loses the non-fast-forward race and is rebased onto a new base does
  **not** re-execute the full suite when the tree/diff is provably unchanged (cache
  hit demonstrated in a test).
- The safety property is preserved: a verdict is never reused for a tree/diff that
  actually differs.
- The number of full-suite gate runs for a concurrent fan-out drops measurably
  (recorded before/after).
- An automated test covers the rebase-then-push path reusing a prior green verdict, and
  a negative test proves a genuinely different tree/diff still misses the cache.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The gate must remain evidence about the **pushed** commit: a verdict may only be
  reused when the tested content is provably identical to what is pushed.
- No weakening of the release gate for `dev`/`main`; `scope=full` stays mandatory.
- Cannot rely on changing per-project suite runtime or sharding.
- Out of scope: redesigning the git transport retry policy for auth/transport failures.

## Existing state

- `.githooks/pre-push` runs `run_tests.py --scope full --gate-commit <sha>` for
  `dev`/`main` pushes and mirrors gate cache entries into the main checkout's
  `.worklog/cache`.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` keys cached verdicts with `fingerprint_kind="tree"`
  and records `gate-subject` / `gate-verdict` provenance (`tree=`, cache hit/miss + age).
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` raises a recoverable non-fast-forward error
  carrying a `rebase_cmd` hint, so the caller rebases onto `origin/dev` and retries —
  producing a new tree and therefore a cache miss today.

## Desired change

A rebased push of provably unchanged content reuses the existing green verdict, so a
lost push race no longer costs another full-suite run.

## Impact

Losing a push race in a concurrent batch costs seconds instead of another five-minute
full-suite run, so a batch's total gate time stops multiplying with the number of
rebases.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — tree-keyed verdict cache, `--gate-commit` binding, `gate-verdict` provenance
- `.githooks/pre-push` — gate invocation and cache mirroring for dev/main pushes
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `PUSH_FAILURE_NON_FAST_FORWARD`, the non-fast-forward exception and its `rebase_cmd` retry path
- `skill/test/tests/` — gate cache/reuse tests to extend
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — push retry / gate documentation

## Related work

- Parent epic: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1)
- Tree-keyed gate verdict (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV) — the cache this item extends.
- Defer full suite to dev-push (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81) — why the gate exists.
- Git transport is fragile under concurrent agent runs: transient SSH auth failures and push races make leaf finish fail after the work has landed (SA-0MW22SEMV00230O5) — push-race handling prior art.
- Sibling item: Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock (SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4) — both reduce gate cost under concurrency.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (safety):** reusing a verdict for a different diff would let an untested change
  reach `dev`; mitigation: reuse only on provable content equality, with a negative test.
- **Risk (scope creep):** batching dev advancement is a larger refactor; treat it as the
  fallback option, preferring the verdict-keying change.
- **Assumption:** a pure rebase produces an identical diff (so a change-set key would
  hit) even though the tree SHA differs.
- **Assumption:** the pre-push hook can be told the intended verdict key without
  weakening the "evidence about the pushed commit" property.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required for this item. Evidence: 21 rebase events and the
2–3-round repeats (AH-0MWEZZE5U, AH-0MWEYVRUX) in the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis on the
parent epic (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1, comment SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR). Researched in the
repository: `.githooks/pre-push` gate invocation and cache mirroring,
`run_tests.py` tree-keyed cache, and the non-fast-forward rebase-and-retry path in
`implement.py`.

# Eliminate no-op drive retries that spawn and immediately give up

Parent: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1).

## Problem statement

In the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis, **9 of 36** implement sessions were effectively
no-ops: 3 messages, ~50 s each — a driven child session that started, loaded the skill,
and exited without doing work (repeated for several child ids, e.g.
AH-0MWEXIWBO004GHN6, AH-0MWEXJ7VJ007XTCQ, AH-0MWEZZ9TE001577J, AH-0MWF0CSSI007P414).
Each is cheap individually but indicates the driver is re-spawning children whose work
is blocked or already done, wasting session startup and muddying the pipeline.

## Users

- **Operator** running `/skill:implement <parent>` drive chains: wants every spawned
  session to do real work.
- **Parent (epic) session** that spawns child sessions and must not waste fan-out slots.
- **Child session** that today starts only to discover there is nothing to do.

User stories:

- As an operator, I want the driver to skip children that are already terminal, blocked
  or held, so a batch spends its slots on real work.
- As a parent session, I want each spawned child session to be startable, so the drive
  report is a faithful record of work done.

## Goal

As an operator, I want the driver not to spawn a child session that will immediately
no-op, so fan-out slots and time are not spent on empty runs.

## Acceptance criteria

- Root cause identified for the no-op spawns (already-terminal child, blocked child, or
  an id collision).
- `phase_drive` does not spawn a session for a child that is terminal/blocked/held, with
  a test covering the observed pattern.
- Re-running the same batch produces zero no-op sessions.
- An automated test reproduces the observed no-op pattern (terminal/blocked/held child)
  and asserts no session is spawned, alongside a regression test that a genuinely
  startable child is still spawned.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Terminal children are never finished, reset or re-spawned (existing invariant).
- Blocked verdicts must never be overridden: a child held by a producer or an unmet
  dependency edge is a soft wait, not a work item to start.
- `max_child_sessions` / `finish_attempt_limit` bounds stay in force — the fix must not
  introduce unbounded retrying.
- Out of scope: reducing session start-up cost itself (skill loading), and the
  lock/gate performance work in the sibling items.

## Existing state

- `phase_drive` runs `parent` (subprocess-isolated) and spawns a fresh Pi session for
  `next_child`, re-fetching and classifying children via `_is_terminal_child` /
  `_reconcile_spawn_failure` after a failed spawn.
- The blocked verdict already stops the chain **without** spawning (SA-0MVS1QS9J009DGPT),
  so the observed no-ops point at a gap between "what `parent` reported as next" and the
  child's actual state at spawn time (terminal/blocked/held/collision).

## Desired change

Before spawning, `phase_drive` re-validates that the reported `next_child` is genuinely
startable (non-terminal, not blocked, not held) and records the reason instead of
spawning when it is not.

## Impact

Operators stop paying session start-up and pipeline noise for children that do no work,
and a drive report reflects only real sessions — so a fan-out batch's wall-clock is not
padded by empty runs.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` spawn decision, `_classify_child`, `_next_child_to_implement`, `_reconcile_spawn_failure`, `_is_terminal_child`
- `skill/implement/tests/` — drive-mode tests (spawn/no-spawn assertions, child locks)
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — drive recovery regression coverage
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — drive-phase documentation

## Related work

- Parent epic: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1)
- implement drive: run each epic child in an interactive Herdr pane (same tab) (SA-0MVLKHY27005UK40) — pane spawning path.
- Failing finish bound / terminal reconciliation prior art (SA-0MVLJXS7R000XIFL, SA-0MVLJXTYY005XQDV) referenced in `phase_drive`'s contract.
- Blocked-verdict soft wait (SA-0MVS1QS9J009DGPT) — the "do not spawn when blocked" precedent this item extends.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (scope creep):** making spawn decisions optimistic-but-retried would hide the
  real defect; the fix must record *why* a child was skipped.
- **Risk:** a stale `parent` report could cause the driver to skip a genuinely startable
  child, stalling the chain; mitigation: re-fetch the child immediately before the spawn
  decision and keep the existing bounded re-run of `parent`.
- **Assumption:** the no-op sessions were driven by stale/incomplete child state rather
  than by a Pi session-start failure; the root-cause AC must confirm this before fixing.
- **Assumption:** the analysis sample (9 sessions, 3 messages each) is representative of
  driven-child no-ops.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required for this item. Evidence: 9 no-op sessions (~50 s,
3 messages) across AH-0MWEXIWBO004GHN6, AH-0MWEXJ7VJ007XTCQ, AH-0MWEZZ9TE001577J and
AH-0MWF0CSSI007P414, from the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis on the parent epic
(SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1, comment SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR). Researched in the repository:
`phase_drive` and its spawn/reconcile helpers in
`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`.

> **OPEN QUESTION (root cause):** the analysis recorded the symptom, not the mechanism.
> The implementing session must identify which of (already-terminal child, blocked child,
> id collision, spawn-time state change) caused the observed no-ops before changing
> behaviour — the AC makes this an explicit deliverable rather than an assumption.
data.title: Eliminate no-op drive retries that spawn and immediately give up

# Measure the 6-way concurrent finish fan-out and record before/after analysis

Parent: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1).

## Problem statement

The parent epic's outcome is stated as a measurable property: under a 6-way concurrent
`finish` fan-out no session should spend the majority of its wall-clock blocked on the
per-repository lock. Today's baseline (2026-11-13, 36 AI_Hell implement sessions) shows
the opposite — 1.7x effective parallelism, 37% of time in `wait_for_job`, 46 lock-waits
averaging 4.3 min (max 21.5 min). Nothing in the epic's child items produces that final
before/after evidence, so without this item the epic can be declared "done" while the
operator-visible symptom is unverified.

## Users

- **Operator** who decides whether a batch is fast enough and whether a fan-out of 6 is
  safe to run by default.
- **Producer** reviewing the epic: needs recorded evidence, not a claim, that the fix
  worked.
- **Future framework work** relying on the same session-analysis methodology.

User stories:

- As the operator, I want a recorded before/after comparison of the same session
  analysis so I can see whether a 6-way fan-out now finishes in roughly the time of one
  work item.
- As the producer, I want the epic's outcome ACs checked against real session logs
  before the epic is closed.

## Goal

As an operator running up to 6 concurrent implement sessions, I want the epic's
lock-contention targets measured against real session logs and recorded, so the speed-up
is verified rather than assumed.

## Approach

- Re-run the 36-session style analysis (per-session `bash`-wait buckets, lock-wait
  medians/maxima, rebase count, full-suite gate run count) on sessions after the sibling
  fixes land.
- Reuse or extend the session-time analysis capability (SA-0MVIKL8U7003UACM) rather than
  hand-rolling a new analyser.
- Compare against the 2026-11-13 baseline recorded on the parent epic and publish both
  numbers side by side.
- Exercise a genuine 6-way concurrent `finish` fan-out if sessions alone do not reach
  concurrency 6.

## Acceptance criteria

- Measure a 6-way concurrent `finish` fan-out and record that no session spends the majority of its wall-clock blocked on the per-repository lock (median lock-wait per session < 60 s; no single lock-wait > 5 min).
- Record a concrete before/after measurement using the same 36-session style analysis.
- The before/after numbers are posted on the parent epic (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1) and state
  explicitly which sibling items were in effect for the "after" run.
- If the targets are not met, the shortfall is recorded as findings with follow-up work
  items rather than reported as success.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Blocked by all four implementation children of the epic: measuring earlier would not
  reflect the fixes.
- Analysis must reuse the same bucketing definitions as the 2026-11-13 baseline so the
  comparison is apples to apples.
- Session logs are operator data: record aggregate metrics and session ids only, no
  prompt/response content.
- Out of scope: per-project suite runtime trimming, and changing changed-scope test
  selection.

## Existing state

- The 2026-11-13 baseline is recorded on the parent epic (analysis comment) with the
  exact metric definitions: summed session time vs wall-clock span, `bash`-wait share,
  `wait_for_job` bucket, lock refusal/wait counts, rebase events, full-suite gate runs.
- Session logs live under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` (e.g.
  `--home-rgardler-projects-AI_Hell-.worklog-*`); the analysis was ad hoc.
- A session-time analysis skill is tracked separately (SA-0MVIKL8U7003UACM).

## Desired change

The epic's lock-contention target is evidenced by a repeatable, recorded before/after
analysis, and any shortfall becomes visible follow-up work instead of an assumption.

## Impact

The operator can see, in recorded numbers, whether a 6-way fan-out now completes in
roughly the time of one work item — instead of trusting that the fixes helped.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — finish/lock reporting fields consumed by the analysis (`main_checkout_lock` report step, lock-wait metrics)
- `.githooks/pre-push` and `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — gate-run provenance (`gate-subject` / `gate-verdict`) used to count full-suite runs
- `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` — session logs analysed (outside the repository)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — where the measurement method should be documented
- session-time analysis skill (SA-0MVIKL8U7003UACM) — reusable analyser to extend rather than duplicate

## Related work

- Parent epic: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1) — carries the baseline metrics and the target.
- Session-time analysis skill (SA-0MVIKL8U7003UACM) — the analyser this item should reuse/feed.
- Siblings this measurement verifies: Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock (SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4); Finish wait ergonomics (SA-0MWFJS65O005JMJF); Stop rebase-induced full-suite re-runs on dev pushes (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC); Eliminate no-op drive retries (SA-0MWFJSCPT005BO2R).
- Post-fix slot-wait re-measurement (SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K) — precedent for a measurement-only follow-up item.
- Audit skill: reduce audit wall-clock time (SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S) — prior session-time analysis methodology.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** measuring before all siblings land produces a misleading "no improvement"
  verdict — mitigated by the explicit blocked-by edges and by naming which items were in
  effect.
- **Risk (scope creep):** turning this into a general performance dashboard is out of
  scope; it is a one-off verification with a reusable analyser where one already exists.
- **Risk:** ambient machine load skews wall-clock comparisons; mitigation: report the
  bucketed metrics (lock-wait counts/medians, gate-run counts), not just totals.
- **Assumption:** comparable session logs (similar work-item sizes) are available for the
  "after" run; if not, a synthetic 6-way fan-out provides the measurement.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required. Evidence: the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell 36-session
analysis and the operator decisions recorded on the parent epic (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1,
comment SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR) — concurrency target up to 6, per-project suite trimming
out of scope. Researched in the repository: the `main_checkout_lock` report step in
`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, gate provenance in `.githooks/pre-push` /
`run_tests.py`, and the session-log layout under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`.
